feature_description: The WebUI backend is a single Tcl CGI (/api/homematic.cgi) that dispatches JSON-RPC 1.1 calls through a flat registry (methods.conf, privilege levels NONE/GUEST/USER/ADMIN) to one Tcl script per method (about 183 scripts in 19 namespaces). Methods reach the system through XML-RPC to rfd/hs485d (tclrpc.so), ReGa script execution (tclrega.so) and direct exec. Sessions and user levels live in ReGa; legacy backup CGIs and eq3_old libraries provide a second auth surface. All outcomes are HTTP 200 with error.code in the body. Classic and nextGen UI are expected to consume this contract side by side.

control_flows.summary: POST JSON-RPC lifecycle: lighttpd CGI -> homematic.cgi sets 'central' (25-30), loads tclrpc.so/tclrega.so (35-39), sources eq3 libs (41-46), builds INTERFACE_LIST (53) and METHOD_LIST (56) -> reads body (141) -> jsonrpc_parse -> getMethod -> array set args -> [central: checkPrivilegeLevel -> getupl.hms via rega_script] -> checkArguments -> source methods/<script>.tcl -> jsonrpc_response; any Tcl error is converted to error 200 with errorInfo; jsonrpc_error exits | Also: Privilege gate for every method in this partition: homematic.cgi runs eq3/getupl.hms against args._session_id_ and compares with the methods.conf LEVEL before sourcing the script.
control_flows.migration_impact: Defines the v1 contract that must be frozen: envelope, error codes (100/102/103/200/400/401/402), ordering (privilege check before argument check), raw id echo, HTTP 200 for all errors Privilege matrix in methods.conf is the effective access policy for both UIs.

control_flows.summary: Authentication/session creation: JSON API Session.login and backup login.cgi both POST tbUsername/tbPassword to http://127.0.0.1/login.htm (ReGaHss-served), read the Location header 'sid=@<id>@', and return the inner id; later calls pass the id in params (_session_id_) or query (sid) and validation is delegated to ReGa's system.GetSessionVarStr; privilege level is session-string field 1 | Also: Session.login: Tcl CGI performs a loopback HTTP POST to ReGa's login.htm, reads the sid from the 302 Location header and returns it; 503 and missing sid map to errors 503/501.
control_flows.migration_impact: Session store and login logic live in closed-source ReGaHss; the API only brokers them. The '@' wrapping inconsistency (A-S7) must be pinned by a contract test Authentication is delegated to the classic login.htm page; any nextGen login must keep this contract or replace it; classic UI keeps using it.

control_flows.summary: Event queue: Event.subscribe takes the lock, creates/empties /tmp/event/<sid>, prunes dead subscribers, registers {EVENT_COUNT 0}, fires 'init'; producers (hm_deldev, subscribe) call event_fire which appends to each subscriber's file up to 64 events; Event.poll reads and clears the file; Event.unsubscribe deletes file and entry; lock is never effective (lock_tryget returns 1) | Also: Event queue: Event.subscribe truncates own queue, loads subscriber.list, (broken) validity-checks other sessions via missing common/checksid.hms, registers own id with EVENT_COUNT 0, fires 'init'; producers (event_fire, called from hm_deldev) append {TYPE DATA} lines to /tmp/event/<sid> while EVENT_COUNT < 64; Event.poll reads and clears its file; Event.unsubscribe removes file and list entry; lock_tryget never blocks
control_flows.migration_impact: Push events (v2) would replace or wrap this polling queue; v1 semantics (type/data records, 64 limit without reset, no producers except delete/init) have to be preserved or consciously changed The existing queue is a polling-only, per-session file mechanism with a path bug that drops other subscribers; a push-event v2 must either replace or coexist with it because the classic UI (www_source/webui/js/homematic/event.js:24-50) still subscribes and polls. Fixing the bug changes eviction behavior for concurrent sessions.

control_flows.summary: Backup CGI lifecycle: <name>.cgi sources common.tcl (loads tclrega/tclrpc, sources session.tcl and rega.tcl) -> startup: parseQueryString, main -> main validates sid via session_isValid == 'false', emits headers, runs XML-RPC/ReGa/file IO -> any error: put_error prints 'HTTP/1.0 400 Bad Request' + text/plain + message
control_flows.migration_impact: Legacy endpoints used by rfd-config style clients; not on the nextGen UI path, but their unrestricted file read and fail-open validation fall within the 'close privilege gaps' goal

control_flows.summary: Classic UI per-page authorization: page script sources session.tcl (legacy) -> read_sessions -> mode detection (sid vs icsessionid) -> session_requestisvalid(needed_upl) -> either ReGa-mirrored path (session_getsessiondata_ise, GetSessionVarStr, session mirrored into SESSIONS.dat) or file path with 900 s timeout; failure renders a stub page and returns negative code
control_flows.migration_impact: Classic UI stays (long-term coexistence); the nextGen UI must not depend on or break this layer, including SESSIONS.dat and the shared ReGa session

control_flows.summary: GET /api/homematic.cgi renders the method documentation page directly from METHOD_LIST without authentication
control_flows.migration_impact: Machine-readable schema (v2) would sit beside or supersede this page; the HTML page is public today

control_flows.summary: Interface.* passthrough: POST -> jsonrpc_parse -> method lookup in methods.conf -> privilege check via getupl.hms (central only) -> required-argument check -> dispatch.tcl resolves args(interface) against INTERFACE_LIST (from /etc/config/InterfacesList.xml, cached in /var/tmp/api_ipc.cache) -> sources methods/<METHOD_FILE> -> xmlrpc via tclrpc.so to rfd/hs485d/HmIPServer -> checkXmlRpcStatus -> hand-built JSON via jsonrpc_response; any uncaught Tcl error becomes JSON-RPC 200 'internal error:\n<errorInfo>'
control_flows.migration_impact: Every Interface.* contract (names, argument names including misspellings such as 'inteface', unquoted-number serialisation, 601 collapse of XML-RPC faults) is part of the frozen v1 behavior; new nextGen endpoints must either preserve or deliberately version these deviations because classic UI keeps calling them.

control_flows.summary: ReGa-script methods (Device.*, Channel.*, Interface.get/set/removeMetadata): hmscript wraps every args entry as a ReGa 'var <sanitised-name> = "<escaped value>"' prefix, runs the script via rega_script, reads STDOUT, parses it as a Tcl list/dict and builds JSON; script errors yield empty output which is mapped to null, '""', or 500 'homematic script error' depending on the method | Also: ReGa query pattern used by SysVar/Program/Room/Subsection/User methods: build a HomeMatic script, inject params as 'var name = "..."' prefixes (hmscript_escapeString/sanitizeIdentifier), run via rega_script, parse the Tcl-list-style output and assemble JSON by string concatenation.
control_flows.migration_impact: Empty-output-to-result mapping differs per method (null vs empty string vs 500); a typed v2 contract or schema must document each case, and any new read endpoints must not copy the metadata-writing side effects of listAllDetail. Output shape is defined by string building (several outputs are non-strict JSON); nextGen consumers will need either the same lenient parsing or corrected output.

control_flows.summary: Device.hasLinksOrPrograms: ReGa check for program usage; if none, ReGa check for links; then resolve interface URL by name, list channels, and for each channel > 0 call XML-RPC getLinks and getDeviceDescription to decide whether any link peer lives on a different parent device
control_flows.migration_impact: Mixes ReGa and XML-RPC in one method and fails for interfaces outside the four hard-coded names; any consolidation or new delete-guard endpoint must replicate or deliberately change this decision logic used by the device delete dialog.

control_flows.summary: Install mode: Interface.setInstallModeHMIP converts on/time, then branches on installMode: LOCAL builds a struct whitelist and calls setInstallModeWithWhitelist; ALL calls setInstallMode(on,time); anything else calls setInstallMode(on) with the unchanged on value (set $on 0 bug)
control_flows.migration_impact: The STOP branch behavior is undocumented in callers; a nextGen inclusion UI must call it with on=false to stop, and any fixed implementation changes outcome for installMode values other than LOCAL/ALL.

control_flows.summary: Gateway configuration rewrite: read existing rfd.conf/hs485d.conf header up to first interface section, truncate file with open w, write header and one section per submitted interface; failures inside the loop set result=false without restoring the file
control_flows.migration_impact: Non-atomic read-modify-write on service config files; edit endpoints exposed to nextGen must preserve the section numbering conventions (RF from 1, Wired from 0) and header retention rules.

control_flows.summary: SSH enable/disable: setSSH touches or removes /etc/config/sshEnabled and sources /bin/setfirewall.tcl, which loads and applies the firewall configuration.
control_flows.migration_impact: Device-facing system integration outside the UI contract.

control_flows.summary: SNMP enable/disable: setSNMPEnabled runs setSNMPUser.sh/unsetSNMPUser.sh, then on success updates the SNMP service access in libfirewall, saves firewall.conf and reconfigures the firewall.
Firmware download: derive product and URL from /VERSION major and board serial, wget over HTTPS to /tmp/fup.tgz, report true/false; error text is stored in /tmp/dwnld.error.
control_flows.migration_impact: Used by the classic maintenance page; nextGen needs the same call.

control_flows.summary: SafeMode.enter: write /etc/config/safemode, persist ReGa objects with rega system.Save() and schedule /sbin/reboot -d 2.
Firewall.setConfiguration: load firewall.conf, replace IPs/user ports/mode/service access from params, save, and apply with Firewall_configureFirewall.
control_flows.migration_impact: Field-name asymmetry (id vs name) between get and set must be preserved or documented.

control_flows.summary: WebUI.getColors merges system color.map with /etc/config/color.map (when central); setWebUIColors seeds, truncates and rewrites the user map line by line.
control_flows.migration_impact: Colour theme shared by classic UI; nextGen theming may reuse or ignore it.

control_flows.summary: Generic Tcl failure path: any uncaught Tcl error inside a method (e.g. missing sysvar, null user, unreadable file) is converted by homematic.cgi into error 200 'internal error:' + errorInfo.
control_flows.migration_impact: Many 'not found' conditions in this partition surface as error 200 rather than a typed error.

user_stories.goal: Dispatch a POSTed JSON-RPC 1.1 request to a registered method script through a fixed pipeline: parse, lookup, privilege check, argument-presence check, source script
requirements: GIVEN REQUEST_METHOD=POST and a body that is a JSON object with a registered method name, a params object containing every name listed in the method's ARGUMENTS, and (when central) a session whose user level >= method LEVEL WHEN homematic.cgi runs THEN it reads exactly CONTENT_LENGTH characters from stdin (line 141), looks the name up in METHOD_LIST (getMethod, lines 87-95), loads params into array 'args' (line 144), runs checkPrivilegeLevel (only if central, lines 147-149), runs checkArguments (line 151) and sources api/methods/<SCRIPT_FILE> in the global scope (line 153); the script emits the response through jsonrpc_response (happy path)

GIVEN a method name not present in methods.conf WHEN getMethod scans METHOD_LIST (lines 90-92) THEN jsonrpc_error 401 "method not found (<name>)" is emitted and the process exits (line 94) (failure path)

GIVEN a registered method whose ARGUMENTS names an argument absent from params WHEN checkArguments runs (lines 127-131) THEN jsonrpc_error 402 "missing argument (<name>)" is emitted for the FIRST missing name in ARGUMENTS order (failure path)

GIVEN any Tcl error raised inside the catch block (parse is excluded because jsonrpc_error exits; includes missing SCRIPT_FILE, method-script runtime errors, odd-length params list, missing CONTENT_LENGTH) WHEN the catch at line 140 fires THEN jsonrpc_error 200 "internal error:\n$errorInfo" is emitted, i.e. the full Tcl stack trace is returned to the client (line 155) (failure path)

GIVEN checkPrivilegeLevel runs before checkArguments WHEN a non-NONE method is called without _session_id_ in params THEN the privilege check fails first with a Tcl error (can't read args(_session_id_)) which surfaces as error 200 and not as 402 (ordering as-is)
edge_cases: WHEN REQUEST_METHOD is neither POST nor GET (PUT, OPTIONS, HEAD...) THEN neither block runs and the CGI emits an empty body with no headers (lines 139, 160)
WHEN REQUEST_METHOD is unset THEN the script dies with a Tcl error before any output (line 139: can't read env(REQUEST_METHOD))

WHEN params is a JSON array with an even number of elements THEN it is silently treated as key/value pairs by 'array set args' (line 144); with an odd number the Tcl error 'list must have an even number of elements' becomes error 200
WHEN jsonrpc_error or a method script calls exit THEN the catch cannot intercept it (Tcl exit is not catchable) and the process ends immediately
WHEN methods.conf is missing or unreadable THEN file_load returns '' (common.tcl:59-69), METHOD_LIST is empty and every call returns 401
WHEN the method script outputs with puts before calling jsonrpc_response THEN that text precedes the JSON envelope (no output buffering or isolation)
WHEN the method name differs only in case from a registry name THEN lookup fails with 401 (string == compare, line 91)
WHEN SCRIPT_FILE comes from methods.conf only THEN the client cannot influence the sourced path (no path traversal via method name)

input_shape.http.method: string, must be POST for this path
input_shape.env.CONTENT_LENGTH: integer string, number of characters to read from stdin; missing -> Tcl error -> error 200
input_shape.body.method: string, exact case-sensitive key of METHOD_LIST
input_shape.body.params: object (flattened to even-length Tcl list); keys become args() element names
input_shape.body.id: optional JSON value, echoed verbatim without re-quoting

output_shape.success: single-line JSON {"id"?: <raw>, "version": "1.1", "result": <method-specific JSON or null>, "error": null} with header CONTENT-TYPE: application/json; charset=utf-8, always HTTP 200
output_shape.error: multi-line JSON {id?, version '1.1', result null, error{name 'JSONRPCError', code integer, message string}} with HTTP 200

user_stories.goal: Load and interpret the methods.conf registry (180 entries) giving LEVEL, SCRIPT_FILE, optional METHOD_FILE, INFO and ARGUMENTS per JSON-RPC method
requirements: GIVEN methods.conf in the CGI working directory (relative path 'methods.conf', homematic.cgi:55) WHEN each request starts THEN the whole file is read and loaded as a Tcl array via file_load + 'array set METHOD_LIST' (lines 55-56); each value is a key/value list with LEVEL, SCRIPT_FILE, INFO, ARGUMENTS (all 180 entries carry all four keys; 49 also carry METHOD_FILE for interface/dispatch.tcl)

GIVEN a method entry WHEN dispatched THEN LEVEL is one of NONE(0), GUEST(1), USER(2), ADMIN(8) as defined in homematic.cgi:58-66; distribution observed in methods.conf: ADMIN 91, GUEST 48, USER 31, NONE 10
GIVEN a LEVEL value not in USER_LEVEL (e.g. a typo) WHEN checkPrivilegeLevel runs THEN 'can't read USER_LEVEL(<x>)' is raised and reported as error 200 (failure path)
edge_cases: WHEN an entry is malformed Tcl (unbalanced braces) THEN 'array set METHOD_LIST' raises at line 56 outside any catch, producing a CGI crash with no JSON envelope
WHEN two entries share a name THEN Tcl array semantics keep the later one (no duplicates exist today: 180 unique names)

WHEN an entry other than NONE omits _session_id_ from ARGUMENTS THEN every call fails with error 200 unless the client supplies _session_id_ anyway; observed for ReGa.getAllDatapoints (methods.conf:483, ADMIN) and Session.setSessionVar (methods.conf:804, GUEST)
WHEN some entries use TAB-indented keys (User.getReGaVersion, line 1239) THEN parsing is unaffected (Tcl whitespace)
WHEN INFO or ARGUMENTS contain non-ASCII ISO-8859-1 characters THEN GET output is declared charset iso-8859-1 (homematic.cgi:161) while JSON output is UTF-8 (jsonrpc.tcl:48)

input_shape.methods.conf: Tcl list text, ISO-8859-1: name {LEVEL <NONE|GUEST|USER|ADMIN> SCRIPT_FILE <relpath> [METHOD_FILE <relpath>] INFO {<text>} ARGUMENTS {<names...>}}

user_stories.goal: Enforce the per-method privilege level by asking ReGaHss for the session's user privilege level (UPL) and comparing it numerically
requirements: GIVEN central=true, a method with LEVEL != NONE and args(_session_id_) of a live ReGa session whose session string is '<uid>;<upl>;...' WHEN checkPrivilegeLevel runs THEN it executes eq3/getupl.hms through hmscript_runFromFile with _session_id_ injected (lines 109-113); getupl.hms returns StrValueByIndex(';',1) of system.GetSessionVarStr(id) (getupl.hms:5-13); if USER_LEVEL(LEVEL) <= upl the request proceeds (happy path)

GIVEN LEVEL ADMIN (8) and a session with upl < 8 WHEN the check runs THEN jsonrpc_error 400 "access denied (\"ADMIN\" needed <upl>)" is emitted (line 115); the number printed is the caller's current upl, not the required one (misleading text, failure path)
GIVEN an unknown/expired session id, or GetSessionVarStr returns empty WHEN the check runs THEN upl stays 0 (getupl.hms:5) so every method above NONE is denied with 400 (failure path)

GIVEN rega_script raises or ReGa is unreachable WHEN hmscript_run catches (hmscript.tcl:33-36) THEN upl="" and the comparison '$level > ""' falls back to string comparison ('1'>'' true), so access is denied with 400 (fail-closed)
edge_cases: WHEN LEVEL is NONE THEN no session lookup happens at all (line 108) and _session_id_ is not required unless listed in ARGUMENTS
WHEN args(_session_id_) is absent for a non-NONE method THEN Tcl error 'no such element in array' -> error 200 with stack trace, not 402 (line 110)
WHEN the session user level is non-numeric (e.g. malformed session string) THEN comparison semantics are Tcl expr string fallback; behaviour not proven by tests
WHEN LEVEL=GUEST (1) THEN any live session with upl >= 1 passes; upl 0 (user level NONE) is rejected
WHEN central=false THEN checkPrivilegeLevel is never invoked (lines 147-149)
WHEN _session_id_ contains quotes/backslashes/newlines THEN hmscript_escapeString escapes them before embedding (hmscript.tcl:62-71)

input_shape.args(_session_id_): string, client-supplied inside params; no format validation

output_shape.denied: JSON-RPC error code 400 message 'access denied ("<LEVEL>" needed <upl>)'

user_stories.goal: Parse the JSON-RPC request body with a hand-written JSON parser into a flat Tcl structure and validate envelope fields
requirements: GIVEN a well-formed JSON object containing method and params (and optionally id) WHEN jsonrpc_parse runs THEN json_parse returns a flat Tcl key/value list, the whole list is converted from UTF-8 (jsonrpc.tcl:24), JSONRPC(METHOD) and JSONRPC(PARAMS) are set and JSONRPC(ID) is set when present, else ID_USED=0 (lines 27-35) (happy path)

GIVEN a body that is not a valid JSON object (missing '{', bad escape, truncated, ...) WHEN json_parse raises THEN jsonrpc_error 100 "invalid request (<parser message>)" is emitted (line 25), e.g. '"{" expected', 'unexpected end of text', 'invaild escape code', '"}" expected', 'number expected' (failure path)

GIVEN a request without a 'method' key WHEN jsonrpc_parse runs THEN error 102 is emitted with message 'params not found in request' (line 31); GIVEN a request without 'params' THEN error 103 with message 'method not found in request' (line 34): code and message texts are swapped relative to the keys (failure path)
GIVEN a request without 'id' WHEN processed THEN ID_USED=0 and the response omits the id member entirely (jsonrpc.tcl:27-29, 52-54, 83-85)
edge_cases: WHEN a value is a number THEN it is kept as the literal text and the template ^-?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)?([eE][+-][0-9]+)? is not end-anchored, so '12abc' yields 12 and leaves 'abc' (json.tcl:161-168); an exponent without sign ('1e5') parses '1' then fails with '"}" expected'
WHEN true/false/null appear THEN they become the literal strings 'true'/'false'/'null', indistinguishable from strings (json.tcl:174-184); json null params arrive as the 4-character string null
WHEN nested objects/arrays are parsed THEN both become Tcl lists with no type tag, so object vs array cannot be distinguished by a method script (json.tcl:43-101)
WHEN text follows the closing brace of the top-level object THEN it is ignored (json_parse, line 36-38, never checks for trailing text)
WHEN a string contains \uXXXX THEN it is decoded with 'subst "\\u$c"' without hex validation (json.tcl:189-198); no surrogate-pair handling
WHEN an object key has no ':' THEN the value defaults to '' instead of raising (json.tcl:56-62)
WHEN the id member is a JSON string THEN the quotes are lost by the parser and the id is echoed unquoted in the response (invalid JSON); only numeric/null ids round-trip (jsonrpc.tcl:53, 84)
WHEN parse fails before the id is known THEN the default JSONRPC(ID) '"error"' is used and ID_USED=1, so the error response carries "id": "error" (jsonrpc.tcl:14-15)
WHEN bytes are UTF-8 THEN stdin is read with default encoding (iso8859-1/system) and re-decoded via 'encoding convertfrom utf-8' on the entire flattened list (jsonrpc.tcl:24)
WHEN the error-table page documents 101 (id missing) and 201-203 THEN these codes are never raised by code

input_shape.request: string (CONTENT_LENGTH chars), JSON object {id?: any, method: string, params: object|array}
input_shape.state.JSONRPC: array with METHOD string, PARAMS list, ID string (default '"error"'), ID_USED 0|1

output_shape.JSONRPC(PARAMS): Tcl list of alternating key/value (values: string | nested list)

user_stories.goal: Serialize JSON-RPC responses and errors with hand-assembled JSON strings and map failures to the documented numeric error codes
requirements: GIVEN a method script that passes a pre-serialized JSON fragment WHEN jsonrpc_response runs THEN the fragment is converted to UTF-8 and embedded verbatim as 'result' on one line: {"id": <id>,"version": "1.1","result": <result>,"error": null} with header 'CONTENT-TYPE: application/json; charset=utf-8'; the script is NOT terminated (lines 72-94) (happy path)

GIVEN jsonrpc_error is called WHEN it runs THEN it prints header, blank line, a multi-line object with version '1.1', result null and error{name 'JSONRPCError', code <raw integer>, message <json_toString text>}, then calls exit (lines 41-67) (failure path)

GIVEN the code space WHEN errors occur THEN codes observed in this partition are 100 (invalid request), 102/103 (envelope, swapped texts), 200 (internal error + errorInfo), 400 (access denied), 401 (method not found), 402 (missing argument); methods add 5xx application codes (e.g. 501/503 in Session.login); documented-only codes: 101, 201-203, 300
edge_cases: WHEN the result string is empty or whitespace THEN 'result' is null (lines 87-91)
WHEN a method script supplies invalid JSON as result THEN it is emitted unvalidated (no serializer)
WHEN a method calls jsonrpc_response twice or after puts output THEN multiple concatenated documents are emitted
WHEN a method never calls jsonrpc_response THEN the CGI ends with only partial or no output (no default response)

WHEN json_toString escapes THEN only " \ / \b \f \n \r \t are mapped; other control characters (U+0000-U+001F) pass unescaped and non-ASCII is emitted raw UTF-8 (json.tcl:204-214); '/' is escaped as '\/'
WHEN error code is not numeric THEN it is emitted raw into the number position, producing invalid JSON (jsonrpc.tcl:60)
WHEN any error occurs THEN HTTP status stays 200; only the JSON error member signals failure
WHEN jsonrpc_error is called twice (e.g. in a nested handler) THEN second call is unreachable because exit is called at line 66

input_shape.jsonrpc_error.errorText: string (any encoding; converted to UTF-8, then JSON-quoted)

user_stories.goal: Inject client-supplied parameters into HomeMatic Script (ReGa) by prepending escaped 'var' declarations and execute the script via rega_script
requirements: GIVEN a method calls 'hmscript {<script>} args' (or hmscript_runFromFile file args) WHEN it runs THEN for every element of the args array a line 'var <sanitized-name> = "<escaped-value>";\n' is prepended (hmscript.tcl:16-19 and 52-55), the script text is appended and executed with rega_script; the returned STDOUT is the result (lines 30-37) (happy path)

GIVEN a value containing backslash, single quote, double quote, newline, CR or TAB WHEN escaped THEN each is prefixed/mapped (\\, \', \", \n, \r, \t) so that the value cannot leave the string literal (hmscript.tcl:63-70)

GIVEN a parameter name containing characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_] WHEN sanitized THEN those characters are removed, a leading char not in [A-Za-z_] gets '_' prepended, and the name is truncated to 64 characters (hmscript.tcl:92-98)
GIVEN rega_script raises (ReGa down, syntax error in script) WHEN hmscript_run catches THEN the empty string is returned and no error is propagated (hmscript.tcl:33-37) (failure path)

GIVEN numeric/boolean parameters WHEN a method uses hmscript_assertFloat/Integer/Boolean THEN 'error "Value '<v>' is not a valid float|integer|boolean"' is raised (hmscript.tcl:73-89), which surfaces as JSON-RPC error 200 (failure path)
edge_cases: WHEN two client param names sanitize to the same identifier (e.g. 'a-b' and 'ab') THEN two 'var' declarations with the same name are emitted; the later array iteration order is Tcl hash order, not deterministic by input

WHEN a client adds an extra param named like a variable used by the method script (e.g. 'id', 'result') THEN it is declared before the script; whether the script's own 'var' redeclaration overrides it is determined by the ReGa interpreter (not verified)
WHEN the whole args array is passed (all methods that call 'hmscript ... args') THEN extra client params, including _session_id_, become ReGa variables
WHEN value contains a NUL byte or other control character THEN it is not escaped (only the six mapped characters are)
WHEN a hmscript_runFromFile filename is relative (e.g. 'eq3/getupl.hms') THEN it resolves against the CGI working directory api/ (file_load, no error on missing file: empty script)

WHEN api/methods/event/subscribe.tcl:25 requests 'common/checksid.hms' THEN that path does not exist under src/webui/www/api (only api/eq3/checksid.hms exists) and the script runs with only the var declaration, returning '' (caller observed: Event.subscribe)
WHEN the function 'hmscript' (lines 10-25) and the file variant (46-60) are used THEN they duplicate the injection logic; hmscript_runInline (39-44) does no injection
WHEN hmscript.tcl is sourced THEN 'package require HomeMatic' (line 8) is executed unconditionally, also in config-tool mode

input_shape.p_args: name of a caller array (string->string) or '-' for none
input_shape.filename: string path relative to cwd (for runFromFile)

output_shape.return: string, STDOUT of the ReGa script; '' when execution failed or produced nothing

user_stories.goal: Provide the shared session library used by the backup CGIs and the PDA UI: login via ReGa's login.htm, validate, renew, resolve user id and logout sessions
requirements: GIVEN valid credentials WHEN session_login POSTs tbUsername/tbPassword to http://127.0.0.1/login.htm without following redirects THEN the Location header is searched for 'sid=@([^@]*)@' and the captured inner id (without the surrounding @) is returned (session.tcl:51-64) (happy path)

GIVEN login.htm answers with HTTP code containing '503' WHEN session_login runs THEN it throws 'create' (too many sessions) (lines 56-58); GIVEN no sid in the Location header THEN it throws 'credentials' (lines 60-62) (failure path)

GIVEN an id that starts with @, ends with @ and has total length 12 WHEN session_isValid runs THEN it executes a ReGa script var _session_id_="<sid>"; ... system.GetSessionVarStr(_session_id_) and returns the script output 'true' or 'false' (lines 74-92)
GIVEN an id failing the shape test (first/last char not '@' or length != 12) WHEN session_isValid runs THEN it returns the string 'false' without contacting ReGa (lines 76-82) (failure path)
GIVEN a valid session WHEN session_logout runs THEN system.ClearSessionID("<sid>") is executed through rega_exec (lines 131-133); for an invalid session nothing happens and no error is raised
GIVEN rega_exec WHEN rega_script raises THEN rega_exec returns '' (rega.tcl:32-40) - so session_isValid returns '' (neither 'true' nor 'false') when ReGa is unavailable
edge_cases: WHEN ReGa fails during session_isValid THEN '' is returned; callers that compare '== "false"' (all api/backup/*.cgi) treat it as valid (fail-open), whereas www/pda/main.cgi:54 compares '{true} !=' (fail-closed)

WHEN the sid is interpolated into the ReGa script (lines 84, 102, 132) THEN it is NOT escaped (unlike hmscript_escapeString); the 12-char shape check limits the payload to 10 arbitrary characters between the two @ signs (quote characters are accepted)

WHEN session_login/ReGa returns the inner id THEN session_isValid insists on '@'-wrapped 12-character ids, while the JSON API passes the inner id to GetSessionVarStr unwrapped (getupl.hms:8-9) and legacy session.tcl:902 uses the short unwrapped form; consistency of ReGa's session key format cannot be proven from source
WHEN session_renew calls http://127.0.0.1/pages/index.htm?sid=@<sid>@ THEN it only cleans up the response; the renewal is a side effect of ReGa serving the page (no validation of result)
WHEN ::http::geturl fails (connection refused) THEN the Tcl error message is propagated; login.cgi maps any other message to LOGIN_ERROR
WHEN session_getUserId is called THEN it does not validate sid shape and returns StrValueByIndex(';',0) or '' (lines 101-109)
WHEN rega_escape (rega.tcl:14-24) is defined THEN it is not used by session.tcl and no other caller was found in src/webui/www except via the backup CGIs sourcing rega.tcl

user_stories.goal: Per-session event queue for Event.subscribe/poll/unsubscribe implemented with files under /tmp/event and a lock file
requirements: GIVEN subscribers recorded in /tmp/event/subscriber.list as a Tcl array id -> {EVENT_COUNT n} WHEN event_fire type message runs THEN, for each subscriber whose EVENT_COUNT < EVENT_LIMIT (64), a line '{TYPE <type> DATA <message>}\n' is appended to /tmp/event/<id>, EVENT_COUNT is incremented, and the subscriber list is rewritten (event.tcl:25-41) (happy path)

GIVEN a subscriber that already has 64 events counted WHEN event_fire runs THEN no further event is queued for it (line 32); the counter is never decremented by Event.poll (poll.tcl:9-16 only reads and clears the queue file), so after 64 events the subscriber receives nothing until it re-subscribes (failure/limit path)
GIVEN homematic.cgi sources event.tcl on every request WHEN /tmp/event/subscriber.list does not exist THEN the directory is created and an empty list file written (event.tcl:49-52)

GIVEN an event producer outside the JSON API WHEN rega/bin/hm_deldev runs THEN it calls event_fire delete "<device>" (src/webui/rega/bin/hm_deldev:17); Event.subscribe fires 'init null' (methods/event/subscribe.tcl:54)
edge_cases: WHEN lock_tryget runs THEN it always returns 1, even when the O_EXCL create failed or the lock file already exists (common.tcl:89-101: 'return 1' at line 100 ignores $result), so there is no mutual exclusion and concurrent CGI processes race on subscriber.list and queue files
WHEN lock_release runs THEN it deletes the lock file unconditionally (common.tcl:106-110), also one held by another process
WHEN a stale lock file exists THEN it does not block anyone (lock is never actually checked)

WHEN Event.subscribe runs THEN it re-validates every other subscriber with hmscript_runFromFile('common/checksid.hms') and deletes subscribers whose result is not 'true' (subscribe.tcl:41-47); because that file path does not exist under api/, every other subscriber is dropped on each subscribe (observed from source, not run)

WHEN the subscriber id from _session_id_ is used as a filename (file join /tmp/event $id) THEN no character validation exists in event.tcl/poll.tcl; protection against '../' relies solely on the privilege check requiring a live ReGa session (central mode); in config-tool mode there is no check
WHEN Event.poll returns events THEN event.DATA is concatenated raw into JSON (poll.tcl:27); the producer must supply valid JSON ('null', '"<dev>"')
WHEN catch swallows an error inside event_fire (line 26) THEN lock_release still runs (line 41) and errors are silent

input_shape.event_fire.message: string, becomes DATA, expected to be valid JSON text

output_shape.queue file line: Tcl list '{TYPE <t> DATA <m>}' per event, newline separated

user_stories.goal: Discover BidCoS/HmIP/etc. interface endpoints from InterfacesList.xml (or BIDCOS_SERVICE in config-tool mode), cache them, and expose them to method scripts as INTERFACE_LIST
requirements: GIVEN /var/tmp/api_ipc.cache is non-empty WHEN ipc_getInterfaces runs THEN the cached array text is returned without re-reading the XML (ipc.tcl:28-34) (happy path)

GIVEN no cache WHEN the interface file /etc/config/InterfacesList.xml is parsed THEN for each <ipc> node having <name>, <url> and <info> children an entry name -> {PORT <port> URL <url> INFO <info>} is built, PORT being the first ':<digits>' of the URL else 0 (ipc.tcl:56-70, 78-84), and the result is written to the cache (lines 30-31)
GIVEN env(BIDCOS_SERVICE) is defined (config tool) WHEN loading THEN a 'default' interface with INFO 'Allgemeine BidCoS-Schnittstelle' is added from it before the XML (lines 45-51)

GIVEN the backup CGIs request an unknown interface name WHEN getInterfaceUrl finds no match THEN it raises UNKNOWN_INTERFACE (backup/common.tcl:31-35), reported to the client as a 400 text response (failure path)
edge_cases: WHEN the cache file exists but is stale (interfaces changed) THEN it is never invalidated or refreshed by code
WHEN InterfacesList.xml is missing THEN file_load returns '' and the interface list is empty (and an empty cache means the file is re-read every time)
WHEN an <ipc> node starts at offset 0 THEN '0 < $node_start' skips it (ipc.tcl:58)
WHEN tags contain attributes or multiple matches THEN simple greedy regexes (.+) are used, not an XML parser (ipc.tcl:61-63)
WHEN /var/tmp is not writable THEN file_save silently does nothing (common.tcl:39-44) and the XML is parsed on every request
WHEN homematic.cgi runs THEN ipc_getInterfaces executes at every request (homematic.cgi:53) even for methods that never use interfaces
WHEN INTERFACE_LIST is consumed THEN only methods/interface/listinterfaces.tcl, dispatch.tcl:158 and device/haslinksorprograms.tcl:14-16 read it (verified by grep)

output_shape.INTERFACE_LIST: Tcl array name -> list(PORT int, URL string, INFO string)

user_stories.goal: Backup CGI framework: query-string parsing, URL decoding, error rendering and the login/logout endpoints used by rfd-config style clients
requirements: GIVEN GET login.cgi?username=U&password=P and valid credentials WHEN main runs THEN session_login returns the sid and the CGI answers 'Content-Type: text/plain' + the inner sid without newline (login.cgi:21-33) (happy path)

GIVEN login fails with 'create' / 'credentials' / any other error WHEN login.cgi catches THEN it raises TOO_MANY_SESSIONS / INVALID_CREDENTIALS / LOGIN_ERROR (login.cgi:24-28), and startup answers 'HTTP/1.0 400 Bad Request', 'Content-Type: text/plain', blank line, error text (common.tcl:93-107) (failure path)

GIVEN logout.cgi?sid=S WHEN main runs THEN session_logout is called and 'OK' is printed (logout.cgi:10-14); an invalid sid is a silent no-op that still prints OK; only a Tcl exception yields the error LOGOUT

GIVEN a QUERY_STRING WHEN parseQueryString splits on '&' and matches '([^=]+)=(.+)' THEN each key/value is URL-decoded (+ -> space, %XX -> char, %0d%0a -> newline) and stored; getQueryArg returns {} for missing keys (common.tcl:38-61, 73-79)
edge_cases: WHEN a parameter has an empty value ('sid=') THEN the regexp (.+) does not match and the key is treated as absent
WHEN credentials are supplied THEN they travel in the query string (GET), appearing in access logs and proxies; the POST body is not parsed for login.cgi (getPostData is used only by run-script.cgi)
WHEN login.cgi documents MISSING_ARGUMENT (header comment lines 9-12) THEN that code is never raised; empty credentials proceed to session_login and fail as INVALID_CREDENTIALS
WHEN login.cgi returns the id THEN it is the inner id without '@'; other backup CGIs require an '@'-wrapped 12-character id (see A-S7), so the client must add the wrappers

WHEN decodeUrl runs THEN %XX sequences are rewritten to \u00XX and run through 'subst -novar -nocommand' then 'encoding convertfrom' (system encoding), backslashes are doubled first (common.tcl:74-76); multi-byte UTF-8 is decoded per byte through the system encoding

WHEN an error is raised after 'Content-Type' was already printed (links.cgi, paramset.cgi, e.g. UNKNOWN_INTERFACE) THEN the response body contains the normal header block followed by the 400 header text inside the body; the HTTP status effectively remains 200 (headers cannot be re-sent)
WHEN backup/common.tcl is sourced THEN the files do 'source common.tcl' relative to the CWD, which requires the web server to run the CGI with its own directory as working directory
WHEN common.tcl loads THEN it loads tclrega.so and tclrpc.so and sources /www/tcl/eq3/session.tcl and rega.tcl with absolute paths (lines 1-5)
WHEN error text is rendered THEN it is Tcl error text (may include file paths) sent as text/plain without sanitization

output_shape.failure: 'HTTP/1.0 400 Bad Request' + text/plain + error token (TOO_MANY_SESSIONS|INVALID_CREDENTIALS|LOGIN_ERROR|LOGOUT|INVALID_SESSION|UNKNOWN_INTERFACE|<Tcl message>)

user_stories.goal: Backup file transfer endpoints binfile/textfile/tarfile/version.cgi: stream an arbitrary server file (or tar of a path) to any authenticated session; report /boot/VERSION without authentication

source.function: main (siblings: textfile.cgi:7-26, tarfile.cgi:7-26, version.cgi:7-11; CR-only line endings)

requirements: GIVEN binfile.cgi?sid=<valid>&file=<path> WHEN main runs THEN session_isValid is checked (line 13), the file is opened and streamed in 32 KiB chunks in binary mode with 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' (lines 8, 15-25) (happy path); textfile.cgi is identical but 'Content-Type: text/plain' (textfile.cgi:18)
GIVEN tarfile.cgi?sid=<valid>&file=<path> WHEN main runs THEN it opens the pipe "|tar c $file" and streams the archive with 'Content-Type: application/x-tar' (tarfile.cgi:15-25)
GIVEN session_isValid returns 'false' WHEN the CGI checks THEN it raises INVALID_SESSION, answered as '400 Bad Request' text/plain (failure path)

GIVEN the file cannot be opened WHEN 'open $file r' fails THEN the Tcl message (e.g. 'couldn't open "<path>": no such file or directory') is returned as the 400 text body before any headers (failure path, binfile.cgi:15)

GIVEN version.cgi WHEN called with no parameters THEN it returns the content of /boot/VERSION as text/plain without newline (version.cgi:8-10); the file is read with loadFile (common.tcl:81-91), '' if missing
edge_cases: WHEN file is any readable path (no allow-list, no normalisation, no privilege level check beyond a live session of any level incl. GUEST) THEN its content is returned; the web server user's file permissions are the only limit

WHEN file contains spaces or Tcl list syntax in tarfile.cgi THEN '|tar c $file' is split as a Tcl list into several tar arguments; option-like values (leading '-') are passed to tar (no '--' separator)
WHEN file is a directory in tarfile.cgi THEN tar recursively archives it
WHEN session_isValid returns '' (ReGa error) THEN the check '== "false"' passes and the file is served (fail-open)
WHEN the pipe closes with non-zero status THEN 'close $fd' raises and the Tcl error text is appended after the already streamed body (line 25)
WHEN file parameter is absent THEN getQueryArg returns {} and 'open {} r' fails with an error
WHEN version.cgi is called THEN no session is required and the file path is /boot/VERSION, whereas tcl/eq3_old/common.tcl:173 reads /VERSION
WHEN these four files have CR-only line endings THEN tools reporting 'wc -l = 0' misclassify them as empty; they are 150-567 bytes and active

input_shape.query.file: string, absolute or relative path, unrestricted

output_shape.error: 400 text/plain token or Tcl error message

user_stories.goal: Backup data endpoints links.cgi, paramset.cgi and run-script.cgi: authenticated dumps of BidCoS links/paramsets and execution of arbitrary ReGa script text
requirements: GIVEN run-script.cgi?sid=<valid> with the script text as POST body WHEN main runs THEN the body is read (common.tcl:63-71), executed with rega_exec and the UTF-8-decoded STDOUT is printed as text/plain followed by a newline (run-script.cgi:9-15) (happy path)

GIVEN links.cgi?sid=..&interface=<name> WHEN main runs THEN it calls XML-RPC getLinks with ('', 0) on the interface URL and prints '[BEGIN LINK]/NAME=/DESCRIPTION=/SENDER=/RECEIVER=/[END LINK]' blocks (links.cgi:7-17, 28-31)
GIVEN paramset.cgi?sid..&interface..&address..&key.. WHEN main runs THEN it fetches getParamsetDescription and getParamset and prints one '<id>:<TYPE>=<value>' line per parameter (paramset.cgi:24-33)
GIVEN an invalid session WHEN any of the three runs THEN INVALID_SESSION is raised and answered with 400 text/plain (failure path)
GIVEN an unknown interface name WHEN getInterfaceUrl runs THEN UNKNOWN_INTERFACE is raised after the Content-Type header was already printed (links.cgi:25-28, paramset.cgi:21-24) (failure path)
edge_cases: WHEN run-script.cgi is called with any valid session regardless of user level THEN the posted ReGa script runs with full ReGa privileges; there is no level check (what ReGa scripts may do, e.g. system.Exec, is not decidable from this source)
WHEN session_isValid returns '' THEN run-script.cgi proceeds to rega_exec, which then also returns '' if ReGa is down
WHEN CONTENT_LENGTH is missing THEN getPostData returns '' (common.tcl:66-70 if-branch skipped) and an empty script is executed
WHEN rega_exec fails or produces nothing THEN the response body is just a newline (rega_exec swallows errors, rega.tcl:34-37)
WHEN the XML-RPC call returns a link lacking NAME/DESCRIPTION/SENDER/RECEIVER THEN 'can't read link(NAME)' aborts mid-response (links.cgi:11-14)
WHEN a parameter id returned by getParamset has no description entry THEN '$types($id)' fails mid-stream (paramset.cgi:32), after earlier lines have been printed
WHEN interface/address/key are passed as XML-RPC strings THEN they are not validated (links.cgi:28 sends fixed args; paramset.cgi:24,30 pass address and key through)
WHEN paramset.cgi declares 'run-script' in its header comment (line 2) and links.cgi header says 'run-script' (line 2) THEN these are copy-paste comments, not behavior

user_stories.goal: Config-tool (non-central) mode: derive 'central' from DOCUMENT_ROOT and switch off ReGa loading and privilege enforcement

WHEN central=false THEN checkArguments still runs (line 151), so argument presence is enforced but session id is not

user_stories.goal: Legacy classic-UI session and privilege layer: file-based sessions in /var/SESSIONS.dat plus ReGa-session mirroring and user level lookup via USERS.dat or ReGa
requirements: GIVEN a classic UI page requiring needed_upl WHEN session_requestisvalid(needed_upl) runs with sidname 'sid' and non-empty sid THEN session_requestisvalid_ise is used (session.tcl:705-707, 869-891): the ReGa session string '<uid>;<upl>;<user>;<first>;<last>;' (regex line 825) is fetched with system.GetSessionVarStr and the page continues only if uid>0 and upl >= needed_upl, else a 'reloadPage' stub is rendered and -4 returned (happy/failure paths)

GIVEN file-session mode (sidname 'icsessionid') WHEN session_requestisvalid runs THEN return codes are -3 (no sid; 'Unauthorized' page), -2/-1/0 (missing/timed-out/unset user; 'Sitzung ungueltig' page), -4 (UPL<0 or < needed; 'zu wenig Rechte' page + timeout reset) or the uid, and valid requests reset the timeout and rewrite /var/SESSIONS.dat (lines 701-754)

GIVEN session_timeout=900 s and MAX_SESSIONS=10 WHEN write_sessions or generatesession runs THEN timed-out sessions are purged (lines 502-523) and a new session is refused with '-1' when 10 exist (lines 13, 16, 476-478)

GIVEN user.tcl in file mode WHEN user_verify/user_upl run THEN credentials are matched in plaintext against /etc/config/USERS.dat lines 'uid;name;password;upl;eq3' (regex user.tcl:47) and only users with eq3==1 are valid (user.tcl:136-169)
edge_cases: WHEN mode detection runs THEN 'sid' mode is chosen if sid appears as URL query parameter 'sid', or POST param, or the current URL contains 'sid=' (session.tcl:762-766); otherwise file-session mode 'icsessionid'
WHEN session_generatesid builds ids THEN rand() * 61 indexes a 62-char alphabet so the last char 'z' is never produced (lines 456-462); length 10 (line 15); rand() is not a cryptographic source
WHEN the sid uniqueness loop runs THEN it relies on catching a failing 'info exists $sessions_uid($sid)' (lines 483, 487) rather than a direct existence test
WHEN passwords are stored THEN USERS.dat holds them in clear text (user.tcl:85-92) and a hard-coded default admin/elv exists but its auto-creation code is commented out (user.tcl:9-11, 69-75)
WHEN read_users_ise is used THEN a fixed placeholder 'blabla' replaces the password (user.tcl:218)

WHEN user_upl_ise/user_name_ise/user_uid_ise/user_isExpert_ise (user.tcl:231-299) interpolate $uid or $uname into ReGa scripts THEN no escaping is applied (injection surface if values are attacker-controlled)
WHEN session_getsessiondata_ise regex captures upl THEN the group is '([0-9])*' (line 825) so only the LAST digit of a multi-digit level is kept (single digit levels 0,1,2,8 are unaffected)
WHEN session_isvalid_ise reports uid<=0 THEN rendered output is the same 'reloadPage' anchor for every failure (lines 876-881)
WHEN tcl/eq3_old files are loaded by classic pages THEN they are symlinked into /www, /www/config, /www/config/display and /www/tools by src/webui/CMakeLists.txt:12-31
WHEN once.tcl sourceOnce is used THEN files are deduplicated by normalized path and fall back to '..' if not found (once.tcl:15-49); common.tcl:2-3 loads cgi.tcl and tclrpc.so once

output_shape.session_requestisvalid: integer: uid (>0 valid), -1,-2,-3,-4 or 0 as documented in comments (lines 424-428, 696-698)
output_shape.side effects: HTML stub pages written to stdout on failure; /var/SESSIONS.dat rewritten

user_stories.goal: Unauthenticated surface of the API partition: everything reachable without a valid session

source.function: GET handler (plus NONE-level methods in methods.conf and backup version.cgi/login.cgi)

requirements: GIVEN any GET to /api/homematic.cgi WHEN handled THEN an HTML page (charset iso-8859-1) lists every method name, privilege label (Gast/Benutzer/Administrator/<keine>), INFO and ARGUMENTS in lsort order, followed by the error-code table (100-103, 200-203, 300, 400-402, 5xx), with no authentication (homematic.cgi:160-215) (happy path)

GIVEN a POST to a LEVEL NONE method WHEN dispatched THEN it runs without session or privilege check; the 10 NONE methods are system.describe (methods.conf:1), system.listMethods (:8), system.methodHelp (:15), system.getEnergyPrice (:35), Interface.isPresent (:225), ReGa.isPresent (:469), Session.login (:783), Session.logout (:790), WebUI.getColors (:959), User.getReGaVersion (:1238)
GIVEN backup/version.cgi and backup/login.cgi WHEN called without session THEN version.cgi returns /boot/VERSION and login.cgi creates sessions (failure path for confidentiality: version disclosure)
GIVEN a request that fails before the privilege check (invalid JSON, unknown method, 401/100/102/103) WHEN answered THEN no session is needed to learn the error contract (failure path)
edge_cases: WHEN the GET listing iterates METHOD_LIST with 'array set method' repeatedly THEN keys are never cleared, so an entry missing a key would inherit the previous entry's value (all 180 entries currently carry all keys)
WHEN Session.logout is NONE-level with _session_id_ argument THEN anyone knowing a session id can terminate it (ClearSessionID, methods/session/logout.tcl:12)
WHEN Session.login fails THEN it distinguishes only 503 ('service not available') from 501 ('invalid credentials or too many sessions') (methods/session/login.tcl:50-56)
WHEN error 200 occurs on any path THEN the unauthenticated caller receives Tcl errorInfo including script paths
WHEN INFO values contain '<' or '&' THEN they are emitted into HTML unescaped (homematic.cgi:190)
WHEN Session.renew and Session.setSessionVar are GUEST-level THEN they require a live session (not part of the unauthenticated set)

input_shape.POST NONE methods: see A-S1; arguments per ARGUMENTS (e.g. username,password for Session.login)

output_shape.GET: text/html; charset=iso-8859-1 document with method table and error code table

user_stories.goal: Route every Interface.* XML-RPC passthrough call through dispatch.tcl: resolve the named interface from INTERFACE_LIST, source the per-method script, map XML-RPC/Tcl status codes to JSON-RPC 5xx/6xx errors, and expose interface discovery (listInterfaces) and liveness (isPresent)
requirements: GIVEN an Interface.* method whose methods.conf SCRIPT_FILE is interface/dispatch.tcl and args.interface names a key of INTERFACE_LIST WHEN the method is called THEN dispatch.tcl loads that entry into the array 'interface' (PORT, URL, INFO) and sources methods/<METHOD_FILE> (dispatch.tcl:156-162)

GIVEN args.interface is not a key of INTERFACE_LIST WHEN any dispatched Interface.* method is called THEN jsonrpc_error 500 with message 'unknown interface (<name>)' is returned and the script exits (dispatch.tcl:158-160)

GIVEN a method script wraps an xmlrpc call as checkXmlRpcStatus [catch {xmlrpc ...}] WHEN catch returns 0 THEN processing continues and the method emits its normal jsonrpc_response (dispatch.tcl:132-133)

GIVEN catch returns a non-zero status WHEN checkXmlRpcStatus runs THEN a JSON-RPC error is returned by status: 1->601 'TCL error', 2->602 'TCL return', 3->603 'TCL break', 4->604 'TCL continue', -1->501 'XML-RPC: general error', -2->502 'XML-RPC: unknown device or channel', -3->503 'XML-RPC: unknown paramset', -4->504 'XML-RPC: device address expected', -5->505 'XML-RPC: unknown argument or value', -6->506 'XML-RPC: operation not supported', -10->507 'Transmission pending in HmIP Legacy API', other->599 'unknown error (<status>)' (dispatch.tcl:135-148)

GIVEN a valid session with GUEST level WHEN Interface.listInterfaces is called THEN an array of {name, port, info} is returned, one element per INTERFACE_LIST key, with port emitted as an unquoted number (listinterfaces.tcl:15-34; methods.conf:241-247)

GIVEN no session id and level NONE WHEN Interface.isPresent is called with only 'interface' THEN true is returned if xmlrpc system.listMethods succeeds against interface(URL), otherwise false (ispresent.tcl:12-16; methods.conf:225-231)
edge_cases: WHEN an xmlrpc call raises an error inside catch THEN the catch body returns code 1, so the observable error is always 601 'TCL error' unless tclrpc.so itself returns other codes; the XML-RPC fault text is discarded because no result variable is passed to catch (every method script, e.g. getparamset.tcl:17)

WHEN args.interface is absent from the request of a method that lists 'interface' in ARGUMENTS THEN 402 'missing argument (interface)' is returned (homematic.cgi:127-130); Interface.setTeam instead lists the misspelled 'inteface' (methods.conf:365), so a missing 'interface' passes the 402 check and fails at dispatch.tcl:156 with a Tcl read error returned as JSON-RPC 200 'internal error:\n<errorInfo>' (homematic.cgi:154-156)
WHEN Interface.setTeam is called THEN the caller must supply an argument literally named 'inteface' to pass the 402 check, plus 'interface' for dispatch.tcl:156 (methods.conf:365)
WHEN a method script uses a bare jsonrpc_error with 501 (getmastervalue.tcl:23, device/get.tcl:130) THEN the code collides with the XML-RPC 'general error' code 501 above
WHEN an INTERFACE_LIST URL has no ':<digits>' THEN listInterfaces reports port 0 (ipc.tcl:78-84)
WHEN listInterfaces iterates INTERFACE_LIST THEN element order follows Tcl 'array names' order (unspecified), not a stable order (listinterfaces.tcl:18)
WHEN the INTERFACE_LIST entry for the named interface is missing INFO/PORT THEN listInterfaces fails with a Tcl error (200 internal error) (listinterfaces.tcl:25-26)
WHEN Interface.isPresent is called with a bad interface name THEN 500 'unknown interface' is returned (not false) because dispatch resolves first (dispatch.tcl:158)

input_shape._session_id_: string; required by ARGUMENTS for all Interface.* except isPresent; resolves privilege via eq3/getupl.hms
input_shape.interface: string; key of INTERFACE_LIST built from /etc/config/InterfacesList.xml (observed names in source: 'BidCos-RF', 'BidCos-Wired', 'HmIP-RF', 'HmIP-Wired' per device/haslinksorprograms.tcl:16-19)

output_shape.result (listInterfaces): array<{name: string, port: integer, info: string}>

user_stories.goal: Describe and list logical devices/channels/teams from the BidCoS/HmIP interface via XML-RPC and convert the device-description struct to JSON (getDeviceDescription, listDevices, listTeams, addDevice)
requirements: GIVEN a GUEST session and a valid interface and address WHEN Interface.getDeviceDescription is called THEN xmlrpc getDeviceDescription(string address) is called and the struct is serialised to {type,address,paramsets,version,flags,...} (getdevicedescription.tcl:13-17; dispatch.tcl:66-127; methods.conf:105-111)
GIVEN the struct contains CHILDREN (a device) WHEN serialised THEN children plus optional firmware, availableFirmware, updatable, firmwareUpdateState are emitted (dispatch.tcl:78-92)

GIVEN the struct has no CHILDREN (a channel) WHEN serialised THEN parent, parentType, index, aesActive, linkSourceRoles, linkTargetRoles, direction plus optional group, team, teamTag are emitted (dispatch.tcl:93-114)

GIVEN a GUEST session WHEN Interface.listDevices or Interface.listTeams is called THEN xmlrpc listDevices / listTeams is called and each struct is serialised with getDeviceDescription into a JSON array (listdevices.tcl:12-24; listteams.tcl:13-25)

GIVEN an ADMIN session and a serial number WHEN Interface.addDevice is called THEN xmlrpc addDevice(string serialNumber) is called and the returned description of the learned device is serialised (adddevice.tcl:13-17; methods.conf:57-63)
GIVEN the xmlrpc call fails WHEN any of these methods runs THEN the error is mapped by checkXmlRpcStatus (601 for any raised Tcl error) (getdevicedescription.tcl:15)
edge_cases: WHEN the struct contains TEAM_CHANNELS but not the misspelled key TEAM_CHANNELD THEN 'teamChannels' is never emitted: the guard at dispatch.tcl:111 tests TEAM_CHANNELD (typo) while the body at line 112 reads TEAM_CHANNELS

WHEN a required key (TYPE, ADDRESS, PARAMSETS, VERSION, FLAGS, or for channels PARENT, PARENT_TYPE, INDEX, AES_ACTIVE, LINK_SOURCE_ROLES, LINK_TARGET_ROLES, DIRECTION) is missing THEN Tcl raises 'can't read device(<KEY>)' and homematic.cgi returns JSON-RPC 200 'internal error:\n<errorInfo>' (dispatch.tcl:72-101)
WHEN AES_ACTIVE or ROAMING is the string 'true' rather than the integer 1 THEN toJSONBoolean returns false because only the value 1 maps to true (dispatch.tcl:30-36, 98, 121)
WHEN version, flags, index or direction are emitted THEN they are unquoted raw tokens, so a non-numeric value yields invalid JSON (dispatch.tcl:75-76, 97, 101)
WHEN UPDATABLE is present THEN it is emitted as a quoted string, not a boolean (dispatch.tcl:87-89)
WHEN INTERFACE or ROAMING are present (BidCoS-RF devices) THEN they are emitted as ',"interface": <str>' and ',"roaming": <bool>' with a space after the colon (dispatch.tcl:117-122)
WHEN listDevices returns an empty list THEN '[]' is returned (listdevices.tcl:14-22)
WHEN addDevice finds no device THEN behavior depends on the interface fault code (see B-S1); no local handling exists (adddevice.tcl:15)

input_shape.address: string; logical device or channel address e.g. 'NEQ0123456:1' (getDeviceDescription)

output_shape.device: {type: string, address: string, paramsets: string[], version: integer, flags: integer, children: string[], firmware?: string, availableFirmware?: string, updatable?: string, firmwareUpdateState?: string, interface?: string, roaming?: boolean}
output_shape.channel: {type: string, address: string, paramsets: string[], version: integer, flags: integer, parent: string, parentType: string, index: integer, aesActive: boolean, linkSourceRoles: string[], linkTargetRoles: string[], direction: integer, group?: string, team?: string, teamTag?: string}

user_stories.goal: Read paramsets, paramset descriptions, paramset ids and single values from a device/channel through XML-RPC (getParamset, getParamsetDescription, getParamsetId, getValue, getMasterValue)
requirements: GIVEN a GUEST session, address and paramsetKey WHEN Interface.getParamset is called THEN xmlrpc getParamset(string address, string paramsetKey) is called and the flat name/value list is serialised to a JSON object with every value as a string (getparamset.tcl:14-29; methods.conf:161-167)

GIVEN a GUEST session WHEN Interface.getParamsetDescription is called THEN each parameter description struct becomes an object {NAME: <param>, <FIELD>: <string>, ...} in a JSON array (getparamsetdescription.tcl:34-57; methods.conf:169-175)
GIVEN a GUEST session WHEN Interface.getParamsetId is called with address and paramsetType THEN the xmlrpc getParamsetId string is returned JSON-quoted (getparamsetid.tcl:14-19; methods.conf:177-183)
GIVEN a GUEST session WHEN Interface.getValue is called with address and valueKey THEN xmlrpc getValue result is returned as a JSON string (getvalue.tcl:14-19; methods.conf:209-215)

GIVEN a GUEST session WHEN Interface.getMasterValue is called THEN the MASTER paramset is fetched and the entry for valueKey is returned as a JSON string (getmastervalue.tcl:17-21; methods.conf:185-191)
GIVEN valueKey does not exist in the MASTER paramset WHEN Interface.getMasterValue is called THEN jsonrpc_error 501 'invalid value key' is returned (getmastervalue.tcl:23)
edge_cases: WHEN address or paramsetKey is unknown to the interface THEN the xmlrpc fault surfaces as 601 'TCL error' (fault text discarded), not 502/503 (getparamset.tcl:17)
WHEN getParamset returns nested/typed values THEN every value is stringified with json_toString, so numbers and booleans are returned as JSON strings (getparamset.tcl:24)
WHEN getParamsetDescription runs THEN parameter order follows Tcl 'array names' (unspecified) and the key NAME is injected as the first field (getparamsetdescription.tcl:42-46)
WHEN getValue returns an empty string THEN jsonrpc_response receives the quoted empty string and the result is '""' (not null) (getvalue.tcl:19)
WHEN Interface.getMasterValue is called THEN no caller-supplied paramset key is used: it always requests 'MASTER' (getmastervalue.tcl:17)
WHEN a GUEST-level caller reads MASTER or any paramset THEN there is no per-address access check (methods.conf:161-167, 185-191, 209-215)

input_shape.paramsetKey: string; 'MASTER' | 'VALUES' | 'LINK' per the method doc (getParamset, getParamsetDescription)

output_shape.getParamsetDescription: array<{NAME: string, TYPE?: string, OPERATIONS?: string, FLAGS?: string, DEFAULT?: string, MAX?: string, MIN?: string, UNIT?: string, TAB_ORDER?: string, CONTROL?: string, VALUE_LIST?: string, SPECIAL?: string}> (field set is whatever the interface returns, all stringified)

user_stories.goal: Write paramsets and single values to a device/channel through XML-RPC (putParamset, putThermParamset, setValue, searchDaliDevices, determineParameter, reportValueUsage)
requirements: GIVEN a USER session and a 'set' array of {name,type,value} objects WHEN Interface.putParamset is called THEN each element becomes [list name [list type value]] and xmlrpc putParamset(string address, string paramsetKey, struct paramset) is invoked, returning true (putparamset.tcl:19-37; methods.conf:272-278)

GIVEN a GUEST session WHEN Interface.setValue is called with address, valueKey, type, value THEN xmlrpc setValue(string address, string valueKey, [type value]) is invoked and true returned (setvalue.tcl:16-23; methods.conf:376-382)

GIVEN a USER session and a 'set' array containing a PARTY_TEMPERATURE entry WHEN Interface.putThermParamset is called THEN the paramset is written to the VALUES paramset of address and true is returned (putthermparamset.tcl:18-41; methods.conf:280-286)
GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.determineParameter is called THEN xmlrpc determineParameter(address, paramsetKey, parameterId) is invoked and true returned (determineparameter.tcl:15-21)
GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.reportValueUsage is called THEN xmlrpc reportValueUsage(address, valueId, int refCounter) is invoked and true returned (reportvalueusage.tcl:15-21)
GIVEN the xmlrpc call faults WHEN any write method runs THEN a JSON-RPC error 601 'TCL error' (or other mapped code, see B-S1) is returned and no true result is produced (putparamset.tcl:35)
edge_cases: WHEN Interface.putThermParamset receives a set without a PARTY_TEMPERATURE element THEN validParamset is never assigned and line 38 raises 'can't read validParamset: no such variable', returned as JSON-RPC 200 'internal error:\n<errorInfo>' (putthermparamset.tcl:31-38)
WHEN a set element lacks name, type or value THEN 'can't read parameter(<key>)' is raised and returned as 200 internal error (putparamset.tcl:27-29)
WHEN type is not one of the XML-RPC types known to tclrpc (doc: string,int,double,bool) THEN it is passed through unvalidated to xmlrpc (setvalue.tcl:21; putparamset.tcl:30)

WHEN GUEST-level callers invoke Interface.setValue THEN actuators can be driven without USER rights because LEVEL is GUEST (methods.conf:376-377); Interface.putParamset needs USER (methods.conf:272-273)

WHEN Interface.searchDaliDevices runs THEN it behaves as setValue without checkXmlRpcStatus: errorMessage is the catch result variable, so any non-empty xmlrpc return value or error text is appended to /tmp/searchDali.log via exec echo and the script calls 'exit' without sending any JSON response (searchdalidevices.tcl:23-31); it is registered at GUEST level (methods.conf:384-390)
WHEN Interface.searchDaliDevices succeeds with an empty errorMessage THEN true is returned (searchdalidevices.tcl:33)
WHEN refCounter is not numeric THEN xmlrpc int conversion fails with 601 (reportvalueusage.tcl:19)
WHEN putThermParamset's set contains several elements THEN all are sent, PARTY_TEMPERATURE only has to appear once (putthermparamset.tcl:23-36)

input_shape.set: array<{name: string, type: string, value: string}> (putParamset, putThermParamset)
input_shape.type: string; XML-RPC type token string|int|double|bool (setValue, searchDaliDevices)

output_shape.searchDaliDevices on failure: no response body; process exits after logging

user_stories.goal: Manage direct device links: create, remove, list, read/write link name+description, list peers, activate link paramsets and assign teams (addLink, removeLink, getLinks, getLinkInfo, setLinkInfo, getLinkPeers, activateLinkParamset, setTeam)
requirements: GIVEN a GUEST session and address (channel address or empty string) and flags WHEN Interface.getLinks is called THEN xmlrpc getLinks(string address, int flags) returns link structs serialised as [{name,description,flags,sender,receiver[,senderParamset][,receiverParamset]}] (getlinks.tcl:51-84; methods.conf:145-151)

GIVEN flags request paramsets (GL_FLAG_SENDER_PARAMSET 0x02, GL_FLAG_RECEIVER_PARAMSET 0x04) and the interface returns SENDER_PARAMSET/RECEIVER_PARAMSET WHEN getLinks is serialised THEN those paramsets are appended as nested objects of stringified values (getlinks.tcl:33-45, 70-76)

GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.addLink is called with sender, receiver, name, description THEN xmlrpc addLink is invoked with four strings and true returned (addlink.tcl:16-23; methods.conf:65-71)
GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.removeLink is called with sender and receiver THEN xmlrpc removeLink is invoked and true returned (removelink.tcl:14-19)

GIVEN a GUEST session WHEN Interface.getLinkInfo is called with senderAddress and receiverAddress THEN {name, description} is returned (getlinkinfo.tcl:16-24); an ADMIN session can write them with Interface.setLinkInfo(sender,receiver,name,description) returning true (setlinkinfo.tcl:16-23)
GIVEN a GUEST session WHEN Interface.getLinkPeers is called THEN the XML-RPC list of peer addresses is returned as a JSON string array (getlinkpeers.tcl:14-28)

GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.activateLinkParamset is called with address, peerAddress and longPress THEN xmlrpc activateLinkParamset(string, string, bool) is invoked and true returned (activatelinkparamset.tcl:15-21)

GIVEN a required argument such as address is missing WHEN any Interface link method is called THEN the dispatcher returns error 402 ('missing argument') before the script runs; GIVEN the interface XML-RPC call fails WHEN getLinks, addLink or removeLink run THEN checkXmlRpcStatus returns error 601 'TCL error' and the XML-RPC fault text is discarded
edge_cases: WHEN Interface.setTeam is called THEN the XML-RPC call is built with the literal strings 'channelAddress' and 'teamAddress' ([list string channelAddress] [list string teamAddress], no $ dereference), so the caller-supplied addresses are read into variables but never sent (setteam.tcl:14-17); the method is registered with ARGUMENTS 'inteface' (typo) (methods.conf:365)
WHEN getLinks flags value is non-numeric THEN xmlrpc int conversion fails with 601 (getlinks.tcl:54)
WHEN a link struct lacks NAME, DESCRIPTION, FLAGS, SENDER or RECEIVER THEN a Tcl read error becomes 200 internal error (getlinks.tcl:64-68)
WHEN link FLAGS is not numeric THEN invalid JSON is emitted because FLAGS is unquoted (getlinks.tcl:66)
WHEN getLinks address is '' THEN links for the whole interface are requested (getlinks.tcl:7 doc, 54)
WHEN getLinkInfo returns no NAME or DESCRIPTION key THEN Tcl read error -> 200 internal error (getlinkinfo.tcl:21-22)
WHEN longPress is JSON true THEN it arrives as the string 'true' and is passed as [list bool true] without normalisation (activatelinkparamset.tcl:17,19)

input_shape.address: string; channel address or '' (getLinks), logical address (getLinkPeers, activateLinkParamset)
input_shape.name: string

output_shape.getLinks: array<{name: string, description: string, flags: integer (0x01 sender broken, 0x02 receiver broken), sender: string, receiver: string, senderParamset?: object<string,string>, receiverParamset?: object<string,string>}>

user_stories.goal: Control device inclusion and device lifecycle on the interface: install mode (on/off, whitelist/local key), search, key-mismatch query, delete/replace device, clear/restore config cache
requirements: GIVEN an ADMIN session, installMode=LOCAL, address, key, keymode WHEN Interface.setInstallModeHMIP is called THEN xmlrpc setInstallModeWithWhitelist(bool on, int time, array[struct{ADDRESS,KEY,KEY_MODE}]) is invoked and true returned (setinstallmodehmip.tcl:55-65; methods.conf:336-342)

GIVEN installMode=ALL WHEN Interface.setInstallModeHMIP is called THEN xmlrpc setInstallMode(bool on, int time) is invoked (key obtained by the interface from the key server) (setinstallmodehmip.tcl:66-68)
GIVEN time is '' WHEN setInstallModeHMIP runs THEN time defaults to 30 seconds (setinstallmodehmip.tcl:38-42)
GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.getInstallMode is called THEN the remaining install-mode seconds from xmlrpc getInstallMode are returned (getinstallmode.tcl:12-14)
GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.searchDevices is called THEN xmlrpc searchDevices returns the number of devices found (searchdevices.tcl:12-14)

GIVEN an ADMIN session and flags WHEN Interface.deleteDevice is called THEN xmlrpc deleteDevice(string address, int flags) is invoked (flags 0x01 reset, 0x02 force, 0x04 defer) and true returned (deletedevice.tcl:17-22; methods.conf:89-95)
GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.changeDevice is called with addressNewDevice and addressOldDevice THEN xmlrpc replaceDevice(old,new) is invoked and true returned (changedevice.tcl:14-19)

GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.clearConfigCache or Interface.restoreConfigToDevice is called with address THEN the like-named xmlrpc is invoked and true returned (clearconfigcache.tcl:13-17; restoreconfigtodevice.tcl:13-17)
GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.getKeyMissmatchDevice is called with reset THEN the serial of the last device that could not be learned is returned (getkeymissmatchdevice.tcl:13-18)

GIVEN a session below ADMIN WHEN Interface.setInstallModeHMIP, deleteDevice or changeDevice is called THEN the dispatcher returns error 400 access denied; GIVEN the interface XML-RPC call fails WHEN deleteDevice runs THEN error 601 'TCL error' is returned without the fault text
edge_cases: WHEN setInstallModeHMIP receives any installMode other than LOCAL or ALL (documented as STOP) THEN line 72 executes 'set $on 0', which assigns a variable named after the value of $on instead of resetting $on, so setInstallMode is called with the original on value; installMode=STOP with on=true therefore switches install mode ON (setinstallmodehmip.tcl:69-74)

WHEN setInstallModeHMIP is called THEN methods.conf requires installMode, interface, on, time, address, key and keymode in ARGUMENTS even for ALL/STOP, so all must be present (possibly empty) to avoid 402 (methods.conf:341)

WHEN on is non-empty and equals 'true', 1 or '1' THEN on=1; anything else (including 'false', '' and other numbers) gives 0 (setinstallmodehmip.tcl:32-36); note setinstallmode.tcl (unregistered) uses a different test (1 == $on or 'true' == $on) (setinstallmode.tcl:14)
WHEN key and keymode are provided in LOCAL mode THEN the key travels in the XML-RPC struct in clear and no validation of key format occurs (setinstallmodehmip.tcl:58-63)

WHEN getInstallMode / searchDevices return an empty value THEN result is null (getinstallmode.tcl:14; searchdevices.tcl:14)
WHEN deleteDevice cannot delete the device THEN the interface fault surfaces as 601 (deletedevice.tcl:20)

user_stories.goal: Firmware refresh/update, service-message counting and suppression, and interface log level (refreshDeployedDeviceFirmwareList, updateFirmware, getServiceMessageCount, suppressServiceMessages, getSuppressedServiceMessages, getLogLevel, setLogLevel)
requirements: GIVEN an ADMIN session and a device serial WHEN Interface.updateFirmware is called THEN xmlrpc updateFirmware(string device) is invoked and its result is converted with toJSONBoolean (true only if the XML-RPC result equals 1) (updatefirmware.tcl:15-19; methods.conf:400-406)

GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.refreshDeployedDeviceFirmwareList is called THEN xmlrpc refreshDeployedDeviceFirmwareList is executed under catch and the method returns toJSONBoolean of the catch status (refreshDeployedDeviceFirmwareList.tcl:15-17)

GIVEN a GUEST session WHEN Interface.getServiceMessageCount is called THEN the number of elements of xmlrpc getServiceMessages is returned as an integer (getservicemessagecount.tcl:13-15; methods.conf:193-199)

GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.suppressServiceMessages is called with channelAddress, parameterId and suppress THEN xmlrpc suppressServiceMessages is invoked and true returned; an empty parameterId suppresses all service parameters of the channel (suppressservicemessages.tcl:16-22)

GIVEN a USER session WHEN Interface.getSuppressedServiceMessages is called with channelAddress THEN the suppressed service parameter ids are returned (getsuppressedservicemessages.tcl:13-28; methods.conf:201-207)

GIVEN a GUEST session WHEN Interface.getLogLevel is called THEN the integer 0-6 from xmlrpc logLevel is returned; an ADMIN session can set it via Interface.setLogLevel(level) which returns the level reported by the interface (getloglevel.tcl:19-21; setloglevel.tcl:20-24)
edge_cases: WHEN refreshDeployedDeviceFirmwareList runs THEN the body is '[xmlrpc ...]' inside catch, so the xmlrpc result string is executed as a Tcl command; catch status 1 is mapped to true by toJSONBoolean, meaning the response is true exactly when catch reports an error (refreshDeployedDeviceFirmwareList.tcl:15-17)
WHEN updateFirmware's XML-RPC result is not exactly 1 THEN false is returned; doc claims per-device array but only a boolean is produced (updatefirmware.tcl:11-19)

WHEN getSuppressedServiceMessages succeeds THEN the already-serialised JSON array is passed through json_toString again, returning a quoted string containing JSON instead of an array (getsuppressedservicemessages.tcl:18-28)
WHEN suppressServiceMessages runs THEN the XML-RPC type token is 'boolean' rather than 'bool' used elsewhere (suppressservicemessages.tcl:20)
WHEN getServiceMessageCount runs THEN it counts all returned service messages, no filtering by suppression (getservicemessagecount.tcl:13-15)
WHEN level in setLogLevel is outside 0-6 THEN validation is left to the interface; no local check (setloglevel.tcl:20-24)

user_stories.goal: Gateway (BidCoS LAN interface) status, assignment, RSSI and AES key plumbing through the interface (listBidcosInterfaces, setBidcosInterface, rssiInfo, getLGWStatus, getLGWConnectionStatus, changeKey, setTempKey, init)
requirements: GIVEN a USER session WHEN Interface.listBidcosInterfaces is called THEN xmlrpc listBidcosInterfaces is invoked and each struct is mapped to {address, description, dutyCycle, isConnected, isDefault, fwVersion, type} (listbidcosinterfaces.tcl:17-44; methods.conf:416-422)

GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.setBidcosInterface is called with deviceId, interfaceId and roaming THEN xmlrpc setBidcosInterface(string, string, bool) is invoked and true returned (setbidcosinterface.tcl:15-21; methods.conf:424-430)
GIVEN a GUEST session WHEN Interface.rssiInfo is called THEN [{name, partner:[{name, rssiData:[a,b]}]}] is built from xmlrpc rssiInfo (rssiinfo.tcl:19-52; methods.conf:320-326)
GIVEN a GUEST session WHEN Interface.getLGWStatus is called THEN {serial, connected} is returned from xmlrpc getLGWStatus (getlgwstatus.tcl:15-20; methods.conf:248-254)

GIVEN a GUEST session and a serial WHEN Interface.getLGWConnectionStatus is called THEN /var/status/<serial>.connstat is read and {connstat: <file content>, serial} is returned (getlgwconnectionstatus.tcl:15-22; methods.conf:256-262)
GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.init is called with url and interfaceId THEN xmlrpc init(string url, string interfaceId) is invoked and true returned (init.tcl:14-19)
GIVEN an ADMIN session WHEN Interface.changeKey or Interface.setTempKey is called with passphrase THEN an xmlrpc call is made and true returned (changekey.tcl:13-17; settempkey.tcl:13-17)

GIVEN a session below the method level (ADMIN for setBidcosInterface, init, changeKey) WHEN the method is called THEN the dispatcher returns error 400 access denied; GIVEN the interface or file access fails WHEN listBidcosInterfaces or getLGWConnectionStatus run THEN error 601 or a Tcl internal error 200 is returned
edge_cases: WHEN Interface.changeKey runs THEN the xmlrpc call has no method name: 'xmlrpc $interface(URL) [list string $passphrase]', so the passphrase is interpreted as the method name argument and the call cannot perform a key change as documented (changekey.tcl:15)
WHEN Interface.setTempKey runs THEN the passphrase is sent as the literal string 'passphrase' ([list string passphrase], no $), not the caller value (settempkey.tcl:15)

WHEN getLGWConnectionStatus receives a serial containing '../' THEN the path /var/status/<serial>.connstat is traversed without sanitisation, limited to files whose names end in .connstat; a missing file raises an open error returned as 200 internal error exposing errorInfo (getlgwconnectionstatus.tcl:17-19)
WHEN getLGWConnectionStatus runs THEN the 'interface' argument is required and validated by dispatch but unused; xmlrpc getLGWStatus is commented out (getlgwconnectionstatus.tcl:14)
WHEN a gateway struct lacks ADDRESS, DESCRIPTION, DUTY_CYCLE, CONNECTED, DEFAULT, FIRMWARE_VERSION or TYPE THEN a Tcl read error -> 200 internal error (listbidcosinterfaces.tcl:29-35)
WHEN listBidcosInterfaces serialises dutyCycle THEN it is a quoted string although documented as integer; isConnected/isDefault are true only for the value 1 (listbidcosinterfaces.tcl:31-33)
WHEN rssiInfo partner data has fewer than two values THEN empty tokens produce invalid JSON like '[,]' (rssiinfo.tcl:39)
WHEN rssiData value is 65536 THEN it means no information (rssiinfo.tcl:16 doc)
WHEN Interface.init runs THEN registration of an arbitrary callback URL at the interface is possible at ADMIN level only (methods.conf:217-223)
